This one hurts.
I want to like this game. I really REALLY want to like this game.
But I don't.
Why?
Becuase the first 1/2-2/3 of this game is good! Very fun, lots of enemy variety and exploring every nook and cranny is a fun and rewarding experience! The bosses for the most part were a great time to smash my head against.
And then i got to the Atlus plains and the game became a boring irritating slog. Almost instantly too. The bosses become repeats of bosses you've already seen, the basic enemies are the exact same as the enemies that you've seen for the last 4 areas, just tankier and hit harder. The game feels like they front loaded it with all of the exciting content then desperately had to fill in the rest of the game with copy and pasted content.
It managed to retroactively dislike previous boss fights by having the exact same boss show up again, and im not talking about some random enemy demon or tree, im talking about storied named bosses that you beat and then they just randomly show up again. There are roughly 10 bosses that you have to fight only once. Out of 170.
It is honestly one of the most frustrating games i've played in where the first 2/3 are really really fun and then you run into a steel wall of disappointment and frustration.
Honestly is worse than Dark souls 1 and 3.

I couldn't even imagine something that marvelous, mysterious, challenging, and yet soothing. This is my first DS game and I'm truly impressed by this dreamlike and true-to-life world at the same time. Sure, it feels like every single creature is eager to slay you while you enjoy the picturesque sceneries, but I've never in my entire life taken such a massive load of screenshots — we must really give credits to the designers of the ER game. There's just one tricky feature — if you want to fully comprehend the plot, I suggest you look through the guides while meeting various NPCs.
To be honest, I was afraid that the game would be too hard to play as the DS games are told to might give you a real hell. Nevertheless, I've managed to walk through ER with a great deal of joy and admiration (it's very comfy to play with a joystick) :)
So if you hesitate whether to buy it or not, I assure you it's worth buying. This game will bring you an incomparable experience and impression for a lifetime! <3

Elden Ring - A Masterpiece in a League of Its Own
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (10/10)

Elden Ring is just GOATED, plain and simple. FromSoftware took everything great about their past games and turned it into one of the most insane open world experiences I’ve ever played. No hand-holding, no forced objectives just pure exploration, discovery, and challenge.

The world design is next level. Every time I thought I’d seen it all, I’d stumble across some underground city, a hidden boss, or a completely new area I somehow missed. It’s the kind of game where you just get lost in the world and don’t even mind.

Combat? Peak. Whether you’re going for a bleed build, tanky greatshield knight, or full-on sorcery spam, the variety is crazy. My endgame character is stacked with weapons, armor, and spells, and I’m still trying out different builds. There’s always something new to mess around with.

And the boss fights? Just ridiculous. Some of the best in any game. Malenia, Radahn, Godfrey, Radagon, each fight feels like an event, where you either get humbled or pull off the sickest clutch win of your life.

This game doesn’t hold your hand, but that’s what makes it so rewarding. Every victory feels earned. Every discovery feels genuine. It’s easily one of the best games I’ve ever played.

Now it’s time for the DLC. Let’s see what fresh hell FromSoft has waiting.

👍 Easy 10/10. Play this game.

This game is all about dying.

Dying because you were out skilled.
Dying because you were under leveled.
Dying because you were ambushed.
Dying because you were outnumbered.
Dying because you fell off a cliff.
Dying because someone left a message telling you to jump.
Dying over and over again against a boss.
Dying inside because you lost runes.
Dying inside because you wasted a consumable on an easy battle.
Dying inside because some fights feel impossible.
Dying at the realization of how large this game is.

But for whatever reason I'm dying every day to keep playing.

Elden Ring isn’t just another open-world RPG—it’s a landmark. FromSoftware took their signature brutal combat and dropped it into a vast, mysterious world that rewards curiosity at every turn. Few games capture the thrill of discovery and the satisfaction of victory like this one.

Yes, repetition creeps in with reused bosses and copy-paste dungeons, but those flaws pale next to the game’s staggering ambition. Each major boss fight feels monumental, each vista breathtaking, and the freedom of playstyle ensures no two journeys are alike.

It’s demanding, it’s relentless, and it’s absolutely unforgettable. Elden Ring didn’t just earn its Game of the Year title—it redefined what an open-world game can be.

Score: 9.5/10

Okay, well, it's a freaking good game, BUT, I still think DS3 is superior.
I have a big misunderstanding about fallen ashes use. If the developers created boss fights, taking into account, that people are going to use them, then they did a bad job balancing this aspect, however, if they thought, that players won't be using them, then why you even bother and add such a mechanic?
Also the invasions are a joke in this game, I've invaded 3 times for a quest and ALL of those times - I've encountered a group of 3 people. In DS2 for ex. I used to invade, and people used to invade to ruin the "boss jogging" for full HP players, so they would have to spend humanity again.
And some of the open world locations are pretty blank and uninteresting, with some of the bosses repeating themselves, however this was an issue in DS1 too, but, like more than 12 has passed and the re-use of assets is still there.
BUT, the capital and the stormveil castle are one of the best, if not THE best locations, throughout the whole series (I haven't played BB, yet. PLS PORT), standing on the same level of design with the Anor Londo.
TLDR: the game has some flaws, but overall they don't matter in the end.
